target_intervention_label: Continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (current 1L)
comment: Holding the FOLFIRI-bev floor is fine as a bridge, but preferences read efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.70 and prefers_trials true, and this patient's only mechanism-matched shot at the A59T driver lives in the codon-agnostic pan-RAS programs (nct:NCT06447662 reads 'any KRAS variant'). Parking daraxonrasib and PF-07934040 out of the top five on a 30% G3+ TRAE that was measured in PDAC on canonical codons (pmid:38778099 is preclinical, the toxicity number is not CRC) treats an unmeasured combination risk as if it were established harm. Bank the NGS and place the sponsor call now so the trial door is open the day 1L stalls.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD, PIK3CA-pathway adjunct
comment: Aspirin is a defensible cheap adjunct, but ranking it first is an evidence-pyramid reflex that mistakes a resected-stage-I-III recurrence HR of 0.49 with a 0.98 upper bound (pmid:40961426) for something that controls active peritoneal stage-IV disease, which it does not. The critic dismisses every pan-RAS agent as 'codon-agnostic structural binding, not efficacy' yet the RAS(ON) glue binds GTP-loaded RAS at a site A59T does not disrupt (pmid:38778099), which is exactly the switch-II biology this atypical allele needs and no other option on the board reaches. For a patient with a real driver and 0.70 efficacy weight, an adjunct that halves recurrence in a different disease setting is not the number-one swing.

target_intervention_label: Comprehensive tumor NGS confirmation
comment: The NGS block is genuinely the day-one move and I do not fight ranking it first, since the A59T VAF and HER2 read gate half of what I want to chase. Where I push: the concensusite files the RevMed/Pfizer sponsor call one rank below the workup as if it must wait, but confirming whether a switch-II A59 allele qualifies on nct:NCT06447662 or nct:NCT07397338 is a phone call that runs in parallel with the panel, not after it. Do not let 'workup first' quietly become 'workup only' and let the trial window drift while 1L runs.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) / codon-agnostic pan-RAS RAS(ON) baskets
comment: Agreed on the ranking and the honesty flag: the pan-RAS RAS(ON) class is the first real shot at A59T and A59T applicability is a structural read-across, not allele-matched data (pmid:38778099). One sharpening, not a disagreement: the NCT07397338 suite mixes codon-selective agents (elironrasib G12C, zoldonrasib G12D) that are mechanism-mismatched to a switch-II A59T, so lead specifically with the codon-agnostic daraxonrasib/PF-07934040 gates (nct:NCT06447662, 'any KRAS variant') rather than the whole basket. Endorse the pick and the sponsor-call-first action.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib / elironrasib / zoldonrasib (RAS(ON)) + ivonescimab ± cetuximab (NCT07397338)
comment: Ranking a RAS(ON) basket first turns an eligibility read into an efficacy claim, and those are not the same thing. The peer-reviewed daraxonrasib data is PDAC on codon 12/13/61 alleles; the CRC monotherapy number is a corporate ORR ~9% with no N and no CI, and A59T sits in switch-II where not one published regression curve exists. The risktaker says this plainly in the concerns, which I credit - but a #1 rank built on structural read-across across a switch-II allele belongs below the FOLFIRI+bev the patient already tolerates and below the one biomarker-matched randomized readout on this board, not above them.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib / elironrasib / zoldonrasib (RAS(ON)) + ivonescimab ± cetuximab (NCT07397338)
comment: The +ivonescimab ± cetuximab arm is where I part company hardest. Daraxonrasib monotherapy already runs G3+ treatment-related AEs around 30% in the PDAC dataset, and stacking a PD-1/VEGF bispecific plus anti-EGFR layers overlapping GI, rash, and hepatic toxicity with zero dedicated combination-toxicity readout in CRC to bound the envelope - and the added VEGF-axis agent is the specific interaction that argues for holding this off until the CRS-HIPEC wound-healing window has passed and a combination-safety readout exists. Not a veto, since preferences carry no toxicity_vetoes, but a firm dissent that the combination arm is uncharacterized rather than merely novel.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) and other RAS(ON) inhibitors on codon-agnostic pan-RAS baskets (NCT06447662 / NCT06445062 / NCT07397338 etc.)
comment: Same objection I raised to the risktaker, with equal force: the advocate's own rationale concedes A59T applicability is a structural read-across pending a sponsor phone call, then ranks it #1 anyway. A codon-agnostic protocol gate is an eligibility question, not evidence the drug works on this allele - the empirical daraxonrasib readouts are all canonical codons and the CRC signal is a ~9% corporate ORR without CIs. Surfacing these trials is fine and the sponsor call is worth making; the rank is the problem, because a mechanism bet with no allele-matched efficacy sits below the standard backbone and below aspirin, not at the top.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO daily as a PIK3CA-mutant adjunct, sequenced around bevacizumab and the CRS-HIPEC bleeding window
comment: This is the one pick where my do-no-harm prior and the advocate land in the same place. ALASCCA (NEJM 2025, n=626, RoB2:Low) hit its primary endpoint with time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (0.24-0.98) in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 Group A that M1043I maps into, and the AE picture is why it clears my bar without hedging - G3+ bleeding ~3% vs 2%, decades of post-marketing data, a fully-mapped management algorithm - with the advocate framing the adjuvant-vs-metastatic gap and the peri-operative bleeding hold honestly. Confirm M1043I is somatic and clonal on the pending NGS before leaning on the Group A match and reintroduce in the post-HIPEC window; beyond that I have nothing to add.

target_intervention_label: Clinical-trial enrollment, biomarker-aligned (pan-RAS and mutant-selective PI3K-alpha programs)
comment: The guideline logic is sound - NCCN routes an A59T/M1043I patient with no on-label match to trial enrollment at category 2A, and I agree the sponsor call confirming the switch-II allele qualifies is high-yield. My qualifier is that the guideline endorses the pathway, not the specific asset, and the rationale reads as if the pan-RAS trials are the obvious destination. Every pan-RAS efficacy readout to date is codon 12/13/61 or a non-CRC tumor, so 'enroll on a trial' and 'enroll on daraxonrasib for A59T' are different claims. Keep the framing at the pathway level and let the characterized options compete for the actual slot.

target_intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab at 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression (Agenus NCT05608044 / CCTG NCT07152821)
comment: I endorse the critic's read here, placement included. Bullock 2024 (Nat Med, n=101) gave ORR 22% in the no-liver-mets subset that is this patient's exact post-resection phenotype, and the randomized update flagged confirmed responses at peritoneal sites - the dominant compartment here - which is the strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal of the modern era. What I want explicit on the record is the toxicity the critic already names: G3+ irAE ~35-38%, immune-mediated colitis 12-13%, hepatitis ~8%, in a patient also facing CRS - an envelope with a codified steroid/infliximab algorithm, which is why this is a right-center, 2L+ pick rather than a first move, exactly where the critic ranked it.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib / RAS(ON) + ivonescimab ± cetuximab (NCT07397338)
comment: Rank 1 rides on the claim that A59T is a plausible extension of the RAS(ON) mechanism, and the row that actually carries A59T is Knox 2025 J Med Chem (pmid:40056080), a drug-discovery paper that tested WT plus G12V/C/D/R, G13D, Q61X and did not test A59T at all — evidence_tier 5, case_match weak in your own dossier. The only peer-reviewed efficacy is Wolpin 2026 NEJM (pmid:42090791), which is PDAC on codons 12/13/61 (2L RAS-G12 ORR 35%, 95% CI 17-56, n=26), and the CRC number you are implicitly leaning on is a Revolution Medicines corporate update at ORR ~9% with no disclosed N, no CI, and no peer review (evidence_tier 4, informal:high). Same structural read-across problem sinks your rank-4 PF-07934040: 'any KRAS variant' is protocol text, not an A59T efficacy readout, and it is a phase-1 dose-escalation on top of that. Ranking a switch-II allele that no trial has ever dosed at the top of the board is a mechanism bet dressed as an eligibility win.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) / RAS(ON) codon-agnostic baskets (PF-07934040, RO7673396, NCT07397338 etc.)
comment: You flag the A59T read-across honestly in the rationale, and I still land on dissent, because the rank does not match what the evidence supports. 'Any KRAS variant' on Pfizer's protocol and the structural argument from Knox 2025 (pmid:40056080, A59T untested) put this at hypothesis-grade for the patient's actual allele; the peer-reviewed daraxonrasib data is PDAC codons 12/13/61 (Wolpin 2026, pmid:42090791), and the CRC monotherapy signal is a corporate ORR ~9% with no N and no CI. Your rank 2, CGT6297, has the cleaner story on paper, an explicit CRC-plus-PIK3CA cohort, but the pharmacology behind mutant-selective PI3K-alpha at a kinase-domain allele lives entirely in breast and gynecologic conference abstracts: RLY-2608 kinase-domain ORR 66.7% (95% CI 38.4-88.2) is ASCO 2025 abstract 1086 in breast plus fulvestrant (informal:high, PMID-null), and tersolisib is ESMO 2024. A protocol slot that names CRC is an eligibility fit, not CRC efficacy, and M1043I is non-canonical relative to the H1047R/E545K data those agents were built on.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO daily as a PIK3CA-directed adjunct
comment: We agree on the substance: ALASCCA is the one RoB2:Low biomarker-matched phase 3 on the board, Group A hit time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98), and M1043I maps into that exon-9/20 stratum. Two corrections keep it honest. First a reference bug you inherited from the dossier: the ALASCCA row is tagged pmid:40961426, which resolves to a corneal-endothelium LATS-kinase paper, not aspirin. The real citation is pmid:40961426 (NEJM, 'Low-Dose Aspirin for PI3K-Altered Localized Colorectal Cancer'), DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2504650. Second, the load-bearing limit is the one you already named. ALASCCA randomized resected stage I-III, and this patient has active stage IV peritoneal disease, so the biology travels but the endpoint does not, which is why it belongs in the post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent window as a layered adjunct rather than antitumor therapy for the metastatic compartment. On your rank 5 botensilimab I would hold the peritoneal-site signal to its grade: single-arm phase 1b (Bullock, pmid:38871975, informal:med) plus a phase 2 whose comparator is monotherapy, with the NLM subset carved out post hoc.

target_intervention_label: Clinical-trial enrollment, biomarker-aligned (pan-RAS and mutant-selective PI3K-alpha programs)
comment: The NGS-first call and the trial-enrollment routing are right, and I agree A59T reads RAS-mutant so anti-EGFR stays closed. My problem is what 'NCCN category 2A' does under the hood here: 2A is lower-level evidence plus uniform expert consensus, not RCT-grade proof, and bundling daraxonrasib (peer-reviewed data is PDAC codons 12/13/61, Wolpin pmid:42090791; CRC mono ORR ~9% corporate; A59T untested per Knox pmid:40056080) with tersolisib and RLY-2608 (breast/gyn abstracts) under the guideline-endorses-trials banner quietly puts single-arm dose-finding on the same shelf as the one RoB2:Low RCT you cite. The category-2A label sanctions the pathway; it does not vet any specific A59T regimen, and the sponsor-confirmation gate you flag is exactly the tell that these are eligibility questions rather than efficacy ones. Also flagging the shared reference bug: your rank-5 aspirin row cites pmid:40961426, which is not ALASCCA — the correct PMID is 40961426 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2504650), and that indication is resected stage II-III, so 'guideline-supported' for this patient's active stage IV disease compresses the same adjuvant-versus-metastatic gap.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib / elironrasib / zoldonrasib (RAS(ON)) + ivonescimab ± cetuximab (NCT07397338)
comment: Ranking a phase-1 RAS(ON) plus PD-1/VEGF-bispecific basket at #1 treats an investigational agent as if it were standard care. NCCN Colon v5.2025 attaches no consensus category to any KRAS A59T regimen; the category-2A endorsement is for trial enrollment as a pathway, not for daraxonrasib or ivonescimab as a therapy. The peer-reviewed RAS(ON) efficacy (pmid:38778099) is codon-12/13/61 preclinical, so a switch-II A59T read-across is a legitimate trial-referral case, not a graded recommendation, and it does not belong above the NGS gate.

target_intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) and other RAS(ON) inhibitors on codon-agnostic pan-RAS baskets
comment: Same guideline problem as the risktaker seat, sharper here because it is rank 1 on codon-agnostic protocol text plus a sponsor call: that is off-guideline for the indication. NCCN Colon v5.2025 routes A59T mCRC to comprehensive NGS (category 1) and trial enrollment (category 2A); daraxonrasib itself carries no category, and its peer-reviewed pivotal readout (Wolpin, pmid:42090791) is PDAC on canonical codons. I endorse it as a trial referral once the workup finishes, not as the day-one move ahead of the NGS that gates it.

target_intervention_label: Anti-EGFR (panitumumab or cetuximab) as an individualized, PI-reviewed question
comment: NCCN Colon v5.2025 and the ESMO mCRC CPG both exclude anti-EGFR for any RAS mutation, and A59T reads as RAS-mutant on extended testing, so panitumumab is off-guideline here whatever the Lochhead n=1 (pmid:28404754) shows. Surfacing it as a PI or tumor-board judgment call rather than pre-closing it is fair, but the honest label is investigational-against-guideline, not a standard option. The Sorich meta-analysis HR 1.08 (pmid:25115304) is the reason the consensus shut this door in the first place.

target_intervention_label: Continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (current 1L), with DPYD/UGT1A1 genotyping
comment: This is the guideline floor and it belongs at rank 1. FOLFIRI + bevacizumab is NCCN Colon v5.2025 category 1 for 1L, the DPYD-before-fluoropyrimidine order tracks the v3.2025 pharmacogenetic update, and the peri-op bevacizumab hold is standard wound-healing practice rather than a research question. No daylight from the consensus seat here.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO daily as a PIK3CA-directed adjunct
comment: Placing aspirin at rank 2, above a reserved cytotoxic backbone, reads it stronger than where the guideline actually put it. NCCN adopted ALASCCA (pmid:40961426) for stage II-III resected PIK3CA-mutant disease as adjuvant therapy; this patient is stage IV with active peritoneal spread, so the 160 mg recommendation is off-label by indication, not consensus-covered for metastatic disease. The conservative row does say this, so I am qualifying rather than dissenting: keep it as a post-HIPEC adjuvant-equivalent add-on with the stage-IV gap spoken plainly.

target_intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance
comment: We land in the same place, and I'll take the qualified agreement, but the fragility read (Group A upper CI 0.98) is the same evidence NCCN weighed before adopting ALASCCA (pmid:40961426) into v4.2025 for stage II-III; a 2A-grade recommendation reflects expert calibration of exactly the CI the critic is reading, so fragile-RCT and guideline-endorsed are both true at once. The guideline-fit point the strict-evidence frame underweights: the binding limiter for this patient is the indication gap, since NCCN's adoption is adjuvant/resected, not the width of the confidence interval. The celecoxib subgroup concordance (pmid:38889377) is why the direction survived that scrutiny.

This is the pick that reads the patient's stated preferences correctly. She weights efficacy at 0.70, wants trials surfaced, declares no toxicity veto and no modality limit - and the atypical A59T is exactly why a codon-agnostic RAS(ON) basket earns rank 1. The prior codon-12/13/61 baskets shut her out; NCT07397338 gates on a documented RAS mutation with no codon named, which is the first door that opens on her actual driver. I share the risktaker's instinct to lead here and to bank the confirmatory NGS that turns the sponsor-eligibility call from a maybe into a yes. Where I hold the line for her: the A59T efficacy gap is real, not rhetorical - every regression curve behind this class is G12/G13/Q61, and the switch-II read-across is mechanism, not an A59T response. The risktaker says that plainly in the rationale, so this is honest advocacy rather than an oversell, and at 0.70 efficacy weight with no veto the class-typical rash/GI burden is a consent conversation, not a blocker.

The DPYD/UGT1A1 safety hygiene and the peri-operative bevacizumab hold are right, and I am not fighting the FOLFIRI-bev floor. My dissent is on where the codon-agnostic pan-RAS trials and the CGT6297 CRC-PIK3CA cohort landed - parked below a reserved FOLFOX-bev 2L backbone that is itself outside Libby's feature-targeting scope. The patient asked for trials to be surfaced, and she carries the one biology - an atypical switch-II A59T - that the new codon-agnostic baskets (NCT06447662, 'any KRAS variant', and NCT07397338) were built to reach. Ranking a second cytotoxic backbone above the first trial that can act on her driver inverts her stated preference set. A do-no-harm posture is defensible in the abstract, but with an empty toxicity_vetoes list and efficacy weighted at 0.70, deferring the on-axis trial referral to a maturity concern reads as the persona's prior, not the patient's. Stage the FOLFOX-bev option, yes - but the trial referral and the sponsor A59T call should sit alongside the backbone, not two ranks under it.

NGS at rank 1 is correct and I will not argue a young metastatic patient into a trial before her extended-RAS and HER2 read is locked. My qualifier is about how the trial pathway gets carried once the workup returns. The concensusite frames enrollment as a category-2A category and keeps the specific slots generic and contingent - but this patient prefers trials, and the two options that actually match her drivers deserve to be named and pushed, not folded into a bucket. The codon-agnostic pan-RAS baskets (NCT06447662's any-KRAS-variant CRC cohort) and the CGT6297 CRC-PIK3CA cohort (NCT07383506, an actual colorectal-and-PIK3CA slot, not a breast read-across) are the on-axis referrals for her A59T and M1043I. 'Trial enrollment is guideline-endorsed' is true but under-serves her; the higher-leverage move she is owed is the sponsor A59T-eligibility call on the named study, made the day the NGS confirms the allele.

This is the right answer to the patient's own sequencing question. She asked for the CRS-HIPEC window to be treated as a constraint and surfaced honestly, and the concensusite gives her the honest version: cytoreduction carries the OS signal, the oxaliplatin HIPEC component did not (41.7 vs 41.2 mo, PRODIGE 7, with more 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm). Keeping the operation and declining to oversell the intraperitoneal drug is exactly the framing she deserves at consent - it lets her weigh the added perioperative burden against a survival gain the randomized data does not show. The one thing I would carry forward for her: the agent choice is not settled either way, so if HIPEC is used, a high-volume center and an explicit conversation about which intraperitoneal agent, timed around her systemic sequencing, keeps this a patient-informed decision rather than a default.

The critic is right on the evidence, and I want to concede it cleanly: aspirin is the one biomarker-matched RoB2:Low phase 3 on the board (ALASCCA, HR 0.49 in the exon-9/20 group M1043I sits in), and the A59T pan-RAS efficacy gap the critic keeps naming is real - those trials rest on codon-agnostic binding, not an A59T response curve. Where I qualify is the ranking lens. Aspirin is a resected-disease adjuvant signal, honestly flagged by the critic as not transferring verbatim to active peritoneal metastatic disease; the patient weights efficacy at 0.70 and prefers trials. For her preference set, a low-cost post-HIPEC adjunct earns a place on the plan but not the top slot ahead of the first trials that can act on her actual driver. So: keep aspirin, layer it in the post-HIPEC window where its evidence lives, and let the codon-agnostic RAS and CGT6297 CRC-PIK3CA referrals sit above it - the evidence pyramid the critic defends and the preference set the patient stated point at different rank orders, and for the advocate seat the preference set wins the tie.

Surfacing anti-EGFR as an individualized, PI-reviewed question rather than a reflexive exclusion is what the patient's surface-everything instruction asks for, and I back it - with the honesty already built into the pick. The A59T-specific case report (pmid:28404754) is a single panitumumab responder, and the Sorich meta-analysis (pmid:25115304, HR 1.08 for OS in the new-RAS subset, n=5,948) is the population signal against it. Neither the risktaker's rank-6 framing nor mine treats the case report as a recommendation; it is a low-probability door the patient is entitled to see with both datasets in front of her, gated on locked extended-RAS/BRAF status. That is the right way to honor 'no reflexive exclusions' without pretending an n=1 outweighs a 5,948-patient null.
